The true infinite iid certificate is transferred to its complete multivariate Mellin fields. Their original nonzero support and all insertion patterns are paid by the actual negative-moment and joint-tail bounds. No analytic or rare probability certificate remains a premise.

Both the bad-proportion tail and the joint tiny-bridge survival tail retain an exponentially small tolerance factor. The remaining inverse-square survival rate pays the complete quadratic pair count, with an explicit sixth-power tolerance cost. Tests may vary with the original prefix length.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.I.description: The two genuine event bounds combine geometrically. The result retains decay both in the complete prefix length on the stopping scale and in the bridge length, without an independence assumption between those events.

The complete output weight is paid by its genuine inserted product moment. A fixed exponent on the original stopping scale is absorbed into survival decay. Cauchy--Schwarz preserves the linear insertion budget.

Only coordinates inside the bridge pay the quadratic Chernoff phase. The complete ambient prefix may be arbitrarily long. Two inserted coordinates cost a fixed factor and the original linear weighted second-norm budget.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.M.description: Finite single, diagonal and ordered double insertions give exact expansions of the complete radial fields. A common signed-test budget pays their full cardinality without scores or omitted coordinates.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.O.description: The true infinite iid certificate is transferred to its complete multivariate Mellin fields. Their original nonzero support and all insertion patterns are paid by the actual negative-moment and joint-tail bounds. No analytic or rare probability certificate remains a premise.

The support retains the genuine certificate and all three cutoff fields. Its bad-proportion and remaining tiny-bridge pieces are measurable and satisfy the exact event containments required by the actual insertion estimates.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.P.description: These estimates keep the original complete product law. A partial sum receives its own Chernoff parameter while every coordinate retains the output weight. Deleting at most two clean moment factors loses at most twice that parameter.

Absolute product densities, rather than scores, pay every weak-test term. The event inverse-square budget gives both integrability of the signed term and its integral bound, including density zeros and diagonal insertions.

The original next-layer normalization is the actual expected reference segment length. Bounded C2 output tests give genuine bounded C2 physical tests, and the convolution increment has the same positive exponential weight with a paid one-gap moment factor.

The inverse moment is paid on the full original coordinate product. In particular the complete physical origin causes no integrability premise in shifted weak tests. All diagonal and ordered cross insertions are retained.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.R.description: Both the bad-proportion tail and the joint tiny-bridge survival tail retain an exponentially small tolerance factor. The remaining inverse-square survival rate pays the complete quadratic pair count, with an explicit sixth-power tolerance cost. Tests may vary with the original prefix length.

The original support is covered by its bad-proportion piece and its remaining surviving tiny bridge. Every insertion pattern of total order at most two is paid on the unchanged measure, including its inverse-square physical factor.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.S.description: The fourth negative moment and the complete original stopping tail combine by Cauchy--Schwarz. The result includes integrability of the weighted event term, and keeps the insertion cost linear in the actual weighted second norm.

The unchanged stopping event is a positive cone. The exact iid marginal and the full Mellin formula transfer its physical derivative, and every signed insertion is paid by the proved actual inverse-square stopping budget.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.W.description: The angular event may be arbitrary. True radial derivatives of the bounded weight pay the cutoff terms. PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.G.description: The actual rank minimum excludes the first two Gamma mixture weights; the unchanged physical second density is C2 at every positive layer.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.W.description: A growing compact bump and a smooth sign approximation test the genuine second density. PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.P.description: The physical output weight theta/C is on the genuine epsilon-squared stopping scale. The uniform mean bracket pays both its fixed-scale cap and its ordinary small-weight cap after theta is fixed. The unweighted second norm is bounded by the same actual weighted second norm.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.F.description: The original core and complementary certificates are summed at the genuine output weight theta/C. The unweighted core cost is paid by the same weighted input norm. All test, moment, negative-moment, and fixed-rate conditions are discharged for the actual reference orbit.

The finite exceptional small prefix lengths have an empty stopping event by the original deterministic minimum segment length. The remaining lengths are paid by the genuine inserted negative-moment estimate, at theta/C.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.P.description: The free cutoff splits into its actual surviving and stopped events. The original convolution increment is C squared times the second derivative of the genuine physical convolution test. The masked long-series bounds pay both one cutoff term and every translated infinite tail.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.A.description: Two genuine global integrations by parts identify the second test under the actual probability law with a test of its actual classical second density. The weighted duality lemma then reads the original weighted second norm.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.O.description: This assembly preserves the actual output law and original cutoff identity. Its two prefix-budget inputs are discharged on that law in the subsequent uniform output theorem; the assembly does not replace the reference process.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.A.description: The free cutoff, full surviving convolution series, and finite stopped correction are all paid by the original core and rare prefix estimates. The one-gap exponential factor and actual normalization are paid uniformly. No analytic recurrence or unproved convolution budget is assumed.

The complete original output weak budget is read against the actual Gamma second density. Compact C2 tests and their smooth sign approximation pay the weighted norm. The recurrence is a theorem of the original reference orbit.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.U.description: The true output recurrence and the actual first-layer initial budget close a fixed polynomial invariant. The measure-level two-thirds scale estimate is therefore unconditional, including the nonsmooth exponential base layer.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Intensit.description: A Model K density is extended by its endpoint values. The extension preserves its original positive bounds and Lipschitz constant. Its cumulative integral is a global order isomorphism; no invertibility premise is imposed on the model.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ArrivalT.description: The intensity primitive and its global inverse define every physical arrival. The cumulative-intensity and restart identities hold pointwise. The physical pair sequence is measurable and its keys are exactly these transformed arrivals.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: Finite common dominating measures give exact density representations. Taking the sum of three probability measures proves the triangle inequality without absolute continuity restrictions. Measurable invertible maps preserve distance.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.BaseGap.description: Its law is the cumulative-intensity inverse applied to a fresh Exp(1) innovation. The original intensity ratio bounds give a uniform exponential moment at one fixed positive parameter, for every physical anchor and every positive intensity.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CountRoute.Local.description: The nonhomogeneous layer comparison applies above a polynomial scale cutoff. The window reduction only needs its exponential tail in that same regime. This module keeps the original height conclusion and original window objects while removing the unnecessary demand for a tail below the layer-comparison cutoff.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: The Jacobian and the actual pushed-forward measure are proved together. The input order isomorphism is globally defined, so there is no missing boundary mass or unproved normalization assumption.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.BaseGapC.description: The normalized cumulative intensity is the inverse of the normalized physical gap. Both are global increasing maps. The pullback exponential density is the actual inverse-gap law, including its complete Jacobian.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.BaseGapQ.description: The error between physical normalization and cumulative-intensity time is an integral of the original intensity variation. Its Lipschitz bound is uniform over anchors and has the required inverse-intensity rate.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: The exponential difference is controlled by the smaller argument and the true Jacobian error by its difference from one. These estimates retain an exponential envelope instead of replacing Hellinger distance by the square root of variation.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ModelKCo.description: Inside the original interval the extended intensity primitive is the original CDF, up to an additive constant. Residual uniform coordinates therefore map to exactly the same physical keys as the actual Poisson arrival construction.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: Linear Jacobian error and quadratic displacement, both of inverse scale order, give an inverse scale Hellinger bound. The proof integrates the actual root densities with a polynomial times exponential envelope.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.BaseHell.description: The true inverse intensity transformation pays both displacement and Jacobian errors. Its Hellinger distance from Exp(1) is of inverse intensity order, with one constant for every physical anchor. The same base law has a fixed uniform exponential moment; no base comparison premise remains.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.LayerObj.description: Every layer is the original endpoint hierarchy applied to the physical arrival sequence. Its state kernel samples the same fresh exponential innovation law. The base layer agrees with the proved Poisson base gap, and the physical output is exactly the key at the original layer pivot.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Intensit.description: Positivity and the original Lipschitz bound control the logarithmic density ratio at every state. Normalization by the reference physical scale introduces exactly the reference span divided by the Poisson intensity.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ChildSca.description: The dilation is the original intensity ratio. Data processing and the proved reference scale regularity pay its Hellinger cost. The only comparison premise is the induction hypothesis for the actual child law at its own anchor.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CompletedPivots.description: The completion test uses the original hierarchy on a zero-tail truncation. Its first successful prefix is an extended natural stopping rank. Causality identifies every finite completion with the original pivot, without assuming that unobserved future segments are finite.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CompletedPivotSt.description: Prefix causality gives an extended stopping rank even when future layers have infinite segments. Finiteness of only the lower layers identifies this rank with the original algorithm; no higher-layer finiteness is assumed.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CompletedPivotRe.description: Two finite completed ranks concatenate to a finite next pivot. The proof works entirely on the observed zero-tail truncation and uses the original pointwise layer restart identity. It does not require future finiteness.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.RestartC.description: Shifting the exponential innovations restarts the same physical arrival sequence at its actual position. At every original endpoint pivot, the shifted layer is exactly the original future layer. These identities are pointwise and do not assume a probability comparison.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.NaturalR.description: The actual physical stopped position is a functional of the stopped prefix. At every almost surely finite natural stopping rank, that position and the fresh innovation sequence have their product law. Applying the actual layer functional gives the original state-dependent Poisson kernel.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Complete.description: The physical arrival transform reads exactly its exponential prefix. The completed endpoint rank therefore is a natural stopping rule, jointly measurable in the physical anchor. Finite ranks coincide with the original hierarchy and admit the proved fresh-innovation restart law.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Successi.description: At a finite completed pivot, the fresh physical sequence has precisely the state-dependent original law. Almost sure finiteness of the leading block at every physical anchor therefore proves finiteness of every successive completed pivot. Higher-layer finiteness is not assumed.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: A jointly measurable conditional density may use a different finite dominating measure at every state. Its actual composition with a marginal density is normalized by kernel Fubini. Kernel Radon-Nikodym derivatives provide these families without assuming absolute continuity to volume.

The conditional reference may depend on the past state and may contain atoms. The conditional squared distance is weighted by the marginal affinity density. This is the same exact chain identity as for product densities, proved by kernel Fubini on the actual composition-product measure.

Every normalized kernel density defines a Markov kernel. Its composition with a marginal density is exactly the measure represented by the joint density, including the full product of Radon-Nikodym factors.

The common conditional reference is the sum of the two actual kernels. Its Radon-Nikodym factors represent the joint laws exactly. Thus the chain identity applies without volume densities, including killed or atomic states.

A nonuniform conditional squared budget is averaged against the two actual past laws. This retains the moment of the physical state and the probability of an active state, rather than replacing them by a global supremum.

The kernels may change at every step and the state may contain the whole observed path. Each conditional budget is integrated under both actual past laws. The exact sums therefore preserve active-state and physical-state moment weights, with no independence assumption on stopping decisions.

The conditional error vanishes on absorbed states. The constant perturbation is paid only by active probabilities; the state perturbation is paid only by active second moments. Both observed-state laws are retained in the exact chain.

A common submeasure contributes its full mass to affinity. Two measurable outputs of the same probability space therefore differ by at most the square root of twice the probability outside any event where they agree.

A state power of exponent at most one is paid by its first and second integer moments. The exact Markov chain budget then gives a cubic finite-horizon cost, without assuming independence of the conditional increments.
The common finite dominating measure pays the density representation. The observable may be unbounded, with its actual second moments on both sides.

A coordinate is sampled from a measurable state-dependent probability kernel. Updating the observed sequence is a common measurable output on both sides. An absorbing decision on the same measurable state set therefore charges exactly the active conditional Hellinger budget.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Ker.description: The observed-state event is retained in the product measure. A bound on each fresh-noise section multiplies its actual probability, which is the conditional step needed for geometric stopping tails.
The joint sampling representation gives both its pointwise law and the composition law under any probability distribution of the observed state.
The observed-state distribution is arbitrary. Integrability and a common nonnegative bound on every conditional fiber pay the composed actual law.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Mom.description: The event may depend arbitrarily on the observable. Its actual probability is retained by the Hilbert-space Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.

The random variable need only be measurable and almost surely nonnegative. No independence is required. Finite sums inherit integer moment bounds from their individual increments by the pointwise power-sum inequality.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Sto.description: Geometric stopping blocks pay the active-step count by one block length. The squared time weight with the square root of the true stopping probability is paid by the cube of that length. These are separate costs in a stopped Hellinger chain, so the constant perturbation retains its linear horizon cost.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CompletedLayerFi.description: Completed ranks increase strictly whenever the later rank is finite. If every completed pivot of a layer is finite, an infinite segment in the preceding original layer would repeat its next pivot, contradicting this strict increase. Thus the conclusion concerns the original hierarchy.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CompletedParentF.description: Only the completed child ranks up to the stopping rank are used. Their finite observed prefixes reproduce the original child keys, so the actual failed prefix also appears in the base truncation. No finiteness of an unobserved parent segment or of a future layer is required.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.GapWindowSurviva.description: The statement is deterministic and applies to the original greedy stopping rule. The window uses its own origin and the same rank tolerance.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.IIDPathMoments.description: The canonical iid sequence is used, rather than an assumed path certificate. Its fixed exponential moment pays every integer cumulative moment and the same moment under the proved finite-prefix kernel iteration.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.IIDPrefixLaws.description: The canonical independent gap law is sampled one coordinate at a time. The entire previously observed finite prefix is independent of its next gap.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.IIDStoppedPrefix.description: The greedy stopping decision is made from the observed prefix. The next iid coordinate remains independent of that prefix, so the stopped path has the same absorbing transition rule as the physical Poisson path.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.FiniteCo.description: The proved physical state law and the canonical iid reference law are compared through their actual coordinate kernels. A fixed conditional exponential moment pays all cumulative second moments, without independence of the physical increments.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Geometri.description: Only the child's completed restarts are assumed finite. A uniform finite window failure probability at all physical anchors is conditioned at the actual child pivot. Surviving long segments contain surviving next windows, which gives the geometric tail without assuming parent finiteness.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.LayerSeq.description: Finite completed ranks identify the observed prefix with the original physical hierarchy. Its greedy stopping rule is unchanged by normalization. The parent output is exactly the stopped sum in the reference parent units.
The original future child sequence restarts at its physical anchor. Its only change of units is the actual intensity ratio, so greedy stopping events are exactly invariant under that ratio.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ParentFi.description: The geometric stopping tail is established while only child completions are known finite. A finite original stopping prefix completes the leading parent pivot; fresh-state restarts then complete all parent pivots and every original child segment.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ParentOu.description: The expected reference span grows by the actual reference compression factor. Hence the original parent gap is precisely the same normalized stopped-sum readout as the true next reference law.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ParentSt.description: The anchor is the actual parent position plus its reference physical scale times the observed cumulative gap. The output dilation is the original intensity ratio. The proved reference scale estimate pays the single-step comparison in terms of that physical cumulative state.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.PathMome.description: Every increment has the original state-dependent gap kernel. A bound at all physical anchors therefore bounds every actual increment marginal. Integer power-sum estimates give cumulative moments without independence.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Positive.description: The original hierarchy sums nonnegative physical gaps, including its defined value on infinite blocks. The intensity bounds pay the fixed-unit dilation of each conditional exponential moment uniformly in the physical anchor.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.PrefixLa.description: The representation uses the original child functional and independent fresh exponential innovations at its natural completed rank. Finiteness of the leading child block at every anchor suffices; parent finiteness is not assumed.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.PrefixSt.description: The state consists of the observed physical child gaps in fixed parent units. It reads only the exponential innovations before the current completed pivot. At every almost surely finite pivot, this entire state is independent of the fresh exponential sequence. Completed ranks retain their infinite value.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.PrefixTr.description: Finite completed pivots identify each observed increment with the original endpoint hierarchy. Its next increment is the fresh child output at the actual physical anchor, dilated into the original parent units.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.StateMom.description: Finite completed pivots identify the cumulative state with the original physical child gap sum. Its conditional exponential budget therefore pays the integer moments used by the Hellinger kernel chain.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.StoppedC.description: The path is the original physical child sequence. Its proved absorbing kernel law, conditional exponential budget, and actual stopping tail pay every finite chain. The common stopped-path map then removes truncation.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.StoppedP.description: The common greedy decision is made on the observed state. Fresh innovations are charged only while active; after stopping the state is absorbed. The law is identified with the original physical prefix stopped by that decision.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowPr.description: The actual original child stopping event is read from its completed prefix. The iid event is read from its canonical prefix. The square-root event inequality transfers the proved finite Hellinger error to a window probability.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedOutput.description: The failed-prefix decision is unchanged by zeroing every later gap, including the extended infinite case. Its original stopped sum is therefore a common measurable output of the full stopped path, and pays no additional Hellinger cost.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedPathCompa.description: The original extended stopping rule defines the common stopped-path map. Its finite observed prefix agrees with the full path whenever stopping has already occurred. Actual geometric tails pay the approximation on each side.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedPrefixMom.description: The original stop may depend arbitrarily on every observed increment. Its nonnegative stopped cumulative sum is bounded pointwise by the full sum at the same deterministic horizon, which pays both integrability and its moment.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedPrefixes.description: The completed failed-prefix decision is retained at every finite horizon. Zero padding after the greedy stopping rank preserves that decision because the original failing keys have already been observed.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedStateBudg.description: Actual geometric tails pay active mass linearly in the block length. Full-path fourth moments pay active second moments cubically. The paid absorbing chain therefore has a uniform bound at every deterministic truncation.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedStateMome.description: The state law is the original stopped child sequence pushed forward to its observed prefix. Both integrability and active second moments are paid from the full path at the same horizon; event dependence is unrestricted.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Additive.General.description: The actual nonhomogeneous Poisson layer comparison, original arrival-window law, exponential block tail and positive span quantile pay both finite-sample window inputs. The conclusion keeps the original density and iid hypotheses, every sufficiently large epsilon, every sample size at least two and the exact universal compression denominator gepC.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CountRoute.Large.description: The optimized Poisson lower-tail bound is evaluated at the actual minimum reference scale. This permits a fixed small physical span quantile while large epsilon makes the count error arbitrarily small.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.L.description: The true first-layer compression has the quadratic epsilon lower bracket. The already proved monotone reference spans propagate that bound through all positive layers, with the epsilon threshold selected before the layer.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowQu.description: Any fixed positive span mass admits a smaller positive rank quantile, a polynomial cutoff constant and a minimum reference scale that pay both the window Hellinger loss and the optimized Poisson count tail.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowSp.description: The actual reference mean and exponential moment pay a fixed lower tail by Paley-Zygmund. The proved uniform polynomial comparison transfers that mass to every actual layer and physical anchor. The exact window-event inclusion then gives the span-quantile premise of the original finite-sample bridge.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: Paley-Zygmund gives a fixed positive mass above one half for a nonnegative mean-one law with a fixed exponential moment. A sufficiently small Hellinger distance transfers a quarter of any reference event mass to the other law.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.U.description: The actual orbit has mean one and positive support. Its proved centered cumulant budget provides a common positive interval on which all raw exponential moments are at most two.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Polynomi.description: The intensity cutoff is expressed with the integer epsilon power 153. The exponential parameter and spatial error constant are fixed first; every prescribed positive Hellinger tolerance is then paid by a fixed cutoff constant, uniformly in epsilon, intensity, anchor and layer.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.SpatialPolynomia.description: A fixed epsilon power 153 suffices for the epsilon-102 weighted two-thirds spatial cutoff. Cubing both nonnegative sides avoids fractional-power constants and preserves the original unrestricted sample-size quantifiers.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.SpatialBudget.description: The two-thirds spatial error is tracked with a fixed polynomial epsilon weight. Quadratic reference compression dominates its linear epsilon propagation factor uniformly above one fixed threshold.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.UniformC.description: All constants are selected from the actual reference orbit and intensity profile before epsilon, intensity, anchor and layer. The proved joint induction closes finiteness, a fixed exponential moment and the two-thirds Hellinger error on every layer inside the monotone comparison cutoff.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.CumulantScaleAri.description: The reference lower compression bound pays both the small conditional tilt and the quadratic cumulant remainder. The geometric window-to-compression ratio pays the stopping compensator at the same fixed positive exponent.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ReferenceScale.G.description: The proved actual-reference stopping tail supplies one window of length ceiling of a fixed multiple of epsilon squared. Its first survival mass is at most one sixteenth, and all multiples have a common geometric bound.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.SpatialD.description: The intensity-profile constant is separated from the two-thirds ratio of the actual reference span to the Poisson intensity parameter. The remaining state factor is exactly the observed cumulative physical gap.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.JointInd.description: The induction is on the original completed Poisson hierarchy and is restricted to a monotone spatial cutoff. Every parent window, tail and moment input is paid by the proved one-layer transfer from the actual child hypothesis. The remaining scalar conditions are uniform parameter choices, separate from the probabilistic induction.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.OneLayer.description: The finite comparison pays the actual window survival probability. True completed restarts pay the geometric stopping tail and parent finiteness. The conditional mean and cumulant then pay the fixed parent exponential moment, while the full stopped-path comparison pays the parent error.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.MeanFrom.description: Actual child exponential moments pay the second-moment observable bound. A sufficiently small Hellinger error then supplies the mean-two budget needed by the conditional parent cumulant.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Hel.description: The second moments on both sides are paid by their true exponential moments. This supplies a uniform conditional mean for a perturbed nonnegative law.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ParentEx.description: The true absorbing-prefix law and the conditional child cumulant pay the compensated stopping potential. The actual geometric stopping tail pays its compensator. The exact parent normalization transfers the resulting moment to the original hierarchy, without an iid assumption on its gaps.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.StoppedExponenti.description: The compensated stopped exponential and the geometric stopping tail are combined by the arithmetic-geometric mean inequality. This argument allows dependent nonhomogeneous gaps and preserves the original stopped readout.

The potential counts only the observed active transitions. Conditional gap exponential budgets suffice; independence of the nonhomogeneous gaps is not assumed. Absorbed prefixes have zero future coordinates.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Conditio.description: The original child-law mean is dilated by the true intensity ratio. The uniform intensity bounds pay its first moment as well as the fixed exponential moment, giving a compensated conditional exponential budget.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.ConditionalExpon.description: The original nonhomogeneous gaps are compared in the physical units of the parent anchor. Their mean need not be one. The quadratic exponential estimate therefore retains the actual uniform mean budget before the stopping argument.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.Comparis.description: The previously paid integer path moments turn a quadratic stopping window into a linear epsilon factor for the child error and an epsilon-cubed factor for the state drift. The same bound applies to the original parent output.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.PolynomialWindow.description: One window length and its cube give the epsilon and epsilon-cubed factors after taking the square root of a path comparison budget.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.QuadraticCompari.description: The constant perturbation has a linear horizon factor and the state drift a cubic horizon factor. A common positive constant pays their square-root sum.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowSp.description: The event of a leading block crossing the actual window is compared with the same normalized layer-gap law proved in the uniform induction. Density ratio bounds pay both event inclusions, including every physical anchor.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.LayerArr.description: On every finite completed leading block the original normalized gap lies between the density-ratio bounds times the exponential arrival sum at its base rank. This connects the proved layer moments to physical window events.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowHe.description: The integrated-intensity window coordinates give exactly the original quantile keys up to the window count. Finite-prefix height therefore reads the completed original leading pivot, without a future-finiteness input.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.FiniteHe.description: A finite prefix is compared with its zero-tail truncation. The original height/pivot equivalence then identifies the event directly with the completed extended-natural pivot, without assuming finite future layers.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.ArrivalW.description: The measurable configuration cut out of the canonical exponential arrival sequence has Poisson count and the proved conditional sorted-uniform kernel. The equality uses the same poissonWindow object as the finite-sample height bridge, with no window-law premise.

The first exponential partial sum above a fixed time defines the window count. Exact disjoint window slices sum to the full Poisson probability mass, proving finite crossing almost surely without adding a divergence assumption. All count fibers and the padded configuration are measurable.

The joint event specifying k arrivals before time s and the normalized arrival coordinates has precisely the Poisson singleton mass times the sorted-uniform coordinate law. Padding and rescaling give the same window kernel used by the original finite-sample bridge.

PLAStochastic.ForMathlib.Probability.Ord.description: Integrating the first arrival after a fixed positive time leaves the constant Janossy density exp(-s) on the ordered arrivals before that time. After normalizing by s the measure is exp(-s) s^k times Lebesgue measure on the closed ordered simplex. This supplies the actual arrival-process window law.

PLAStochastic.Index.KEP.Poisson.WindowEx.description: The fixed exponential moment of the actual normalized layer gap pays the physical window-crossing event by Chernoff. The unconditional polynomial comparison supplies both that moment and true completed-pivot finiteness, at precisely the local cutoff needed by the original height reduction.
